# 2020B Question 11 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

Using opioids as examples [**describe and illustrate**]{.task-verb} with graphs what you understand by the terms "potency", "efficacy", "partial agonist", "competitive antagonist", and "therapeutic index".
:::

Also asked in: [2005B Question 2](/content/exams/anzca/2005/B/2/index.qmd#examiner-comments), [2012A Question 5](/content/exams/anzca/2012/A/5/index.qmd#examiner-comments), [2018B Question 7](/content/exams/anzca/2018/B/7/index.qmd#examiner-comments)

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Describe and illustrate**]{.task-verb} each term with a precise definition, opioid example and labelled graph. Distinguish graded from quantal responses and keep dose or concentration on the horizontal axis.

::: {.structure-headings}
### Potency: Definition, Opioid Example and Graph

### Efficacy: Definition, Opioid Example and Graph

### Partial Agonism: Definition, Opioid Example and Graph

### Competitive Antagonism: Definition, Opioid Example and Graph

### Therapeutic Index: Definition, Opioid Example and Graph
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
It was expected that candidates would provide basic definitions, provide examples to support the definitions, and draw labelled graphs to demonstrating key points.

For the most part this basic pharmacology question was answered well, perhaps because it has been asked before. The examiner’s comments at that time are still relevant. Most candidates were able to give passable definitions, draw correct log dose - response curves demonstrate key points, and correctly use opioids as examples.

Definitions were sometimes worded awkwardly or omitted. Some candidates linked efficacy with intrinsic activity, then neglected to explain either term. An opioid example of therapeutic index was rarely mentioned.
:::
